name: html-inline-button-in-paragraph-becomes-native
description: A paragraph carrying one text-only inline <button> with no form or runtime-behavior semantics converts to editable core/paragraph RichText instead of freezing the whole line as core/html. The button lowers into a <mark> RichText carrier — legal under both RichText's format library and the engine's own editability policy — with its resolved presentation baked into the mark's own style attribute and role="button"/tabindex="0" keeping it labelled and keyboard-reachable, instead of leaving a class-bearing <button> tag neither recognizes.

source_reference.notes: Regression fixture for a base44 React SPA import (posts/page-sellerregister.post_content, selector p.text-center.text-xs.text-muted-foreground): 'Already a seller? <button>Sign in</button>' degraded to core/html, the only quality-gate failure on that source (fallback_count: 0, core_html_block_count: 1). A first attempt (#1992) rode the literal <button> tag through into RichText content and was reverted (#1993) because the engine's own editability policy rejects a structural rich-text attribute tag it does not recognize.

legacy_comparison.reason: New native inline-button-in-paragraph behavior has no legacy equivalent.
